title: How AI Phone Agents Handle Shopify Orders That Ship in Multiple Packages
summary: Learn how AI phone agents handle split Shopify shipments with caller verification, package-level tracking checks, and safe human handoffs.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- When a caller asks why only one box arrived, the phone agent must verify their identity before disclosing any order or tracking details.
- Before answering, the agent must match the order’s[fulfillments, item quantities, and tracking numbers](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/Fulfillment) . One fulfillment can carry multiple tracking numbers, so the agent should not guess which item is in which box.
- The agent should distinguish a package marked delivered from items marked shipped or not yet fulfilled. An estimated arrival date is not a delivery promise.
- If tracking is missing, stale, or mismatched, or the caller disputes a delivery, the agent should stop the automated answer and transfer the call with the verification outcome, available package facts, timestamps, and caller context. The handoff must not include verification secrets.
- This split-shipment call is narrower than[general order-status and returns handling](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/ai-phone-answering-ecommerce-order-status-returns-handoffs) .


## What the caller actually wants to know


A caller who received one box wants to know whether the remaining items shipped separately, are delayed, or are missing. One delivered tracking number cannot answer that question for the whole order.[Shopify allows multiple fulfillments on one order](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/Fulfillment) , and a fulfillment can carry more than one tracking number. A partial delivery may be normal, but the agent cannot assume which items belong in the box that arrived.


Before discussing the remaining items, the phone agent must verify the caller and retrieve the authorized order. The agent then needs to match item quantities to fulfillments, check every associated tracking number, and compare available shipment updates with their timestamps. Only then can the agent report which tracking numbers show delivery and which items belong to the associated fulfillments. It can identify an item as delivered only if a reliable package-to-item record connects it to the delivered box. If the records cannot establish that distinction, the agent should say so and hand the call to a person rather than guess.


## A sample explanation that holds up


Once the caller passes verification, the phone agent can explain each part of the order using matched Shopify and carrier records. The agent should distinguish what Shopify records say about the remaining items from what the carrier reports about each package.


A safe answer for a verified example would be, “UPS tracking for the first package reports delivered on Tuesday. Shopify shows the remaining items have not been marked fulfilled. I can’t confirm when those items will ship.” The agent attributes the delivery report to UPS rather than claiming the caller received the package. It also distinguishes an unfulfilled item from a shipped package.[UPS defines delivered as a tracking status](https://www.ups.com/us/en/support/tracking-support/where-is-my-package/understanding-tracking-status) , which a caller may still dispute.


If a second package has shipped, the agent should report its own tracking status and last scan instead. “Shopify marks the fulfillment shipped, and the carrier has not reported delivery for its tracking number” gives the caller a useful answer without turning a shipping status into a delivery promise. “The rest will arrive Friday” would be unsafe unless a current, authorized source supports that date, and even a carrier estimate should be identified as an estimate.


When carrier data is older than the merchant’s freshness limit, the agent must withhold claims about the package’s current location or expected arrival. It can give the timestamp of the last confirmed update and transfer the caller for review rather than fill the gap with a guess.


## Verifying the caller before disclosing anything


Before an AI phone agent discusses a missing package, the caller must pass a merchant-approved check for access to that specific order. The check applies even when the caller knows which item arrived. Caller ID can be spoofed or shared, and a forwarded receipt can reveal an order number and email address. None of those details alone proves that the caller may hear shipment information.


The agent should request verification without confirming that the order exists or naming its products, recipient, address, or tracking numbers. A merchant might require a code sent to a contact method already associated with the order, but that check needs its own approved configuration. The agent should not treat a caller-provided replacement email or phone number as an authorized destination.


If the check fails or ownership remains ambiguous, the agent should stop before disclosing package details and transfer the caller for human verification. The handoff can state that verification was incomplete, but it must not pass along one-time codes or authentication answers.


## Mapping fulfillments, line items, and tracking numbers


To account for the remaining items, the agent must compare the order's line-item quantities with every fulfillment. After verifying the caller, the agent needs to retrieve the authorized[order and its fulfillments](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/Order) . The order’s overall fulfillment status gives a summary, but the agent must inspect the individual records to answer which items have been marked fulfilled.


Each[fulfillment](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/Fulfillment) lists its fulfillmentLineItems and quantities. Those records let the agent match, for example, one of two ordered shirts to a shipped fulfillment while showing that the second shirt is not included in that fulfillment. The agent should compare quantities across all fulfillments with the order’s line items and check for records beyond the first page before describing what remains.


Tracking numbers require a separate check. A fulfillment’s trackingInfo can contain multiple numbers, so one fulfillment does not necessarily mean one box. If a fulfillment contains a shirt and a mug alongside two tracking numbers, Shopify’s fulfillment record alone does not establish which item went into the delivered box. The agent can report which items belong to that fulfillment and which tracking number shows delivered, but it should not connect a specific item to that box without a reliable package-level record. If the caller needs that distinction and the mapping remains unclear, the agent should transfer the question for review.


## Reading carrier status without overpromising


After verifying the caller, an AI phone agent should read the remaining packages’ statuses separately. Shopify can record when a fulfillment was updated and when a[fulfillment event](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/FulfillmentEvent) happened. Those timestamps answer different questions, so a recent Shopify update does not prove the carrier recently scanned a package. The agent should associate a carrier event with a tracking number only when the available records support that match. If they do not, it should report the uncertainty and transfer the call.


[UPS defines](https://www.ups.com/us/en/support/tracking-support/where-is-my-package/understanding-tracking-status) “Label Created” as receipt of shipment details, not necessarily the package. “On the Way” indicates movement through its network, while “Exception” signals a problem that may change the scheduled delivery date. “Delivered” records a delivery event, but it does not establish that the caller received the parcel. An agent can say, “UPS reports the first tracking number delivered on Tuesday. UPS lists the second tracking number as ‘On the Way,’ but I can't confirm when that package will arrive.” The agent should not turn an estimated date or an earlier scan into a promise.


Your policy should set an acceptable age for both the latest carrier event and the last successful tracking fetch. When either exceeds that limit, the agent should give the time and source of the last confirmed update, say that the current location or delivery date cannot be confirmed, and transfer the caller for review. A quiet tracking page alone does not prove a package is lost.


## When to stop and hand the caller to a person


A phone agent should stop answering when it cannot establish which package the caller means or trust the status it finds. Transfer the call if tracking is missing, if a tracking number does not match the verified Shopify order or the carrier record, or if the latest data falls outside the merchant’s freshness limit. An ambiguous package-to-item mapping also requires a person.


A disputed delivery needs a human review even when the carrier reports “delivered.” The agent can tell a verified caller what the carrier reports and when, but it cannot conclude that the caller received the package. If Shopify and the carrier disagree, the agent should transfer the call. It should share each source's status and timestamp with the receiving person and disclose those details to the caller only if verification succeeded. It should not promise a replacement, refund, or arrival date. If verification fails, the agent must withhold order and shipment details during the transfer as well.


SigmaMind AI’s[documented warm transfer](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/transfer-call) can connect a receiving person first and give them a private whisper before the caller joins. Configure that whisper to include the verification outcome, the authorized order reference when verification succeeded, relevant fulfillment and tracking references, the source and time of the latest status, and the caller’s concern. Include the mismatch or dispute and any checks already attempted so the caller does not have to repeat the problem. Never pass one-time codes, authentication answers, or other verification secrets. Test that the receiving person hears the summary on the merchant’s actual phone route, and set a safe fallback for unanswered or failed transfers.


## Implementation: permissions, data access, and testing


-


**Grant only the Shopify access the call needs.** read_orders covers order and fulfillment reads within Shopify’s default 60-day order window. Older orders require read_all_orders alongside read_orders, subject to Shopify approval. A tracking-only call does not need permission to change an order. Grant read scopes only for the Shopify data the configured lookup actually uses.[Shopify’s order access rules](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/usage/access-scopes#orders-permissions) set these limits.


-


**Separate the connection from the call logic.**[SigmaMind AI’s Shopify setup guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/app-integration/shopify) documents a custom-app path in which you grant scopes and connect a store token. Treat caller verification, authorized order lookup, package mapping, and partial-delivery answer rules as merchant-specific configuration to design and test. The documented connection does not establish a ready-made split-shipment phone workflow.


-


**Check shipment data before the agent speaks.** Confirm that the authorized lookup returns each fulfillment, its line items and quantities, and its tracking numbers.[Shopify’s fulfillment fields](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/Fulfillment) support those distinctions, but carrier updates have no guaranteed freshness in the cited documentation. Set a merchant-specific age threshold for the last usable update, and route the call to a person when tracking is missing, contradictory, or too old to trust.


-


**Test the phone handoff live.** Confirm how your phone system routes calls to and from SigmaMind AI, then test a disputed delivery, an unavailable receiving person, and a failed transfer on the actual route.[SigmaMind AI’s Transfer Call guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/transfer-call) documents warm transfers with an optional private whisper. Review the whisper for the verification outcome, package facts, source timestamps, and caller concern, and remove passwords, codes, tokens, and other verification secrets. If the transfer fails, the agent should say it cannot confirm the remaining shipment and follow your approved fallback rather than guess.


-


**Keep helpdesk setup separate.**[SigmaMind AI’s Gorgias guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/app-integration/gorgias) describes an optional app connection. Test any helpdesk use independently, and use authorized Shopify and carrier records, not Gorgias, to establish shipment facts.


## How this fits with order tracking and returns workflows


For a Shopify brand with substantial phone-support volume, this split-shipment flow answers a specific question about one package arriving before the rest of an order. The agent needs package-level evidence to answer it and a route to a person when that evidence is unclear.


The[ecommerce order-status and returns guide](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/ai-phone-answering-ecommerce-order-status-returns-handoffs) covers broader support calls, including returns and handoffs. If you are choosing an answering service rather than building this call flow, the[Shopify phone-support vendor comparison](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/best-voice-ai-shopify-phone-support) covers that decision. The[Wonderment tracking integration page](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/real-time-tracking-with-wonderment-sigmamind-ai-integration) focuses on a particular tracking-data connection, which you would need to assess separately from caller verification and transfer behavior.


## FAQ


-


**Can the agent tell me which items are in each box?** Only after verifying the caller and checking a reliable package-to-item record. Shopify lists items and quantities by fulfillment, but[one fulfillment can have multiple tracking numbers](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/objects/Fulfillment) . Without a clear item-to-box match, the agent should transfer the question rather than guess.


-


**What if tracking has not updated in days?** The agent should state the last confirmed status and its timestamp, then follow the merchant’s freshness policy.[Carrier updates depend on scans](https://www.ups.com/us/en/support/tracking-support/where-is-my-package) , so a quiet tracking page does not establish a new delivery date. If the data is too old to trust, a person should review it.


-


**What if the carrier says delivered, but I never received the package?** The agent can report the carrier’s dated delivery status, but it cannot confirm that the caller received the box. A person should investigate the dispute. The agent should not promise a replacement or refund.


-


**Does this work when multiple warehouses fulfill one order?** It can, if the merchant's configured lookup provides authorized fulfillment records and sufficiently current tracking data for shipments from each warehouse. The agent must check each shipment separately and transfer the call when records conflict or a warehouse’s shipment details are unavailable.


## Conclusion


A reliable answer to a split-shipment call depends on verified, current package data. After confirming the caller’s identity, the phone agent should match the remaining items to fulfillment and tracking records before describing what shipped or arrived. If those records leave a package’s status unclear, the agent should say what it cannot confirm and transfer the caller with the known facts.
